messages:
lee m: Heads-up: publish-typegen job failed on release/candidate due to a regen diff that removed an 'Example' bullet added by the new sample app. CI shows no semver bump so the pipeline aborted.

build-bot: GitHub Actions · publish-typegen · FAILED
Job: regen-check -> non-empty diff detected
Logs: `CHANGELOG.md: removed line 'Example: retry pattern for auth middleware (sample-app)'`

noor k: ugh. I saw something similar earlier but it was because our new changelog sanitizer collapses duplicate entries. Could be the sanitizer + contributor-sort interaction.

lee m: I pulled the branch. The commit that adds the sample app and CHANGELOG entry exists (sha d4f9b6). Locally: `yarn typegen` produces the line, but running `node ./scripts/changelog-sanitize.js` removes the parenthetical and then a dedupe step drops the line.

miguel s: That dedupe logic was intended to remove copy churn, not user-visible sample references. We need to ensure sample/example bullets survive sanitize.

typegen-bot: typegen v2.5.0 · Generated files changed: CHANGELOG.md; contributors sorted; examples ordered by name

noor k: two-pronged fix: (1) make sanitize smarter: preserve bullets starting with "Example:" or containing "sample"; (2) make semver-bump detect that sanitize removed content and treat that as a visible change. Which do we prefer to land first?

lee m: prefer landing sanitize patch first, it's the source. But short-term unblock: we can add a temporary unique token suffix to the changelog line so dedupe doesn't remove it, then revert. ugly but fast.

miguel s: I'll open PR in tooling: #1514 "chore(sanitize): preserve sample/example changelog bullets". Adding unit test and fixture.

qa-bot: created ticket QA-778: "changelog sanitize strips sample bullets causing semver false-negative" (owner: miguel s)

noor k: also, can we add a regen-diff CI stage that runs typegen + sanitize inside the same container used by publish pipeline, so we replicate the step ordering and catch these locally? Right now we run typegen in one job and sanitize in a later job that uses a different image.

lee m: yes please. I hit this because my local env used a newer node and sanitize behaved differently. A single-container replay would have caught it.

miguel s: I'll include a small script `tools/ci_regendiff_replay.sh` in the PR. It runs: `yarn typegen && node ./scripts/changelog-sanitize.js && git --no-pager diff -- CHANGELOG.md`. Also adding a check to fail the job if post-sanitize diff != 0.

typegen-bot: Created PR #1514 with tests + ci_regendiff_replay.sh.

noor k: great. long-term we should also update semver-bump to compute a "changelog fingerprint" before and after sanitize and consider sanitize delta as a change. But let's not block the release on that.

lee m: for the current release I pushed a temp fix: commit adds ` (preserve-sample)` to the sample line and re-ran publish pipeline. Re-run queued.

build-bot: re-run triggered by lee m: publish-typegen · queued

miguel s: once PR lands I'll follow up to remove the preserve token and revert the temp commit. Also adding docs in devx/release-playbook about sanitize behavior so SDK contributors know why some parentheticals matter.

noor k: one more suggestion: update sample-app generator templates to include a sentinel comment like `<!-- keep-changelog-example -->` so tooling can spot intentional content. Then sanitize can be safely aggressive elsewhere.

lee m: good idea. leaving a note in the onboarding checklist. Thanks folks — please ping release when PR #1514 is merged so I can remove the temp commit. :thumbsup:
